title: The gate's DOC-ONLY fast path looks only at the tip commit (or staged files), so a docs row landing last hides every code commit earlier in the wave
reasoning: Measured 2026-11-20 on main c4cf366 (four code rows AUG-186/189/171/155 landed in a row): 'PATH=.venv/bin:$PATH AUGER_CI=1 CI=1 bash tests/gate.sh' printed '== gate mode: DOC-ONLY fast path (skipping pytest + e2e smoke) ==' and then 'GATE PASS' with 'arms SKIPPED (not passed): pytest, e2e-smoke'. Cause: tests/gate.sh:95-112 sets CHANGED from 'git diff --cached' when anything is staged, else 'git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD' - a single-commit window. The tip commit was the docs-only AUG-155 row, so the AUG-186 auger.py runner change and the AUG-189 gate.sh change were never tested by the gate that declared PASS. The gate must not equate 'the last commit is docs' with 'the tree is docs'.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 FALSIFIER: on a tree where the tip commit changes only docs/ but the preceding commit changes auger.py, 'bash tests/gate.sh' must run the FULL gate (print '== gate mode: FULL gate ==') and its summary must NOT list pytest as SKIPPED. Today it prints the DOC-ONLY fast path and PASS - paste that current output as the red. AC2: the doc-only decision is derived from the whole unreviewed range (e.g. the merge-base of origin/main, or an explicit base argument the caller must supply), not from a one-commit window, and a test in tests/test_gate_mode.sh pins it: a two-commit case, docs on tip and code below, must assert FULL gate. AC3: a genuine docs-only range still takes the fast path in the same self-test, so the rule is proven in both directions (red-prove each arm per verification discipline).
